content.comment_body: Hello, I need to control an induction heater operating between 4kHz and 8kHz using analog inputs and digital outputs on a [product_name]. Is there a way to accomplish this, possibly with expansion modules? Any advice is appreciated. Kind regards, [user_name]

This setup won't be feasible using the [product_name] PLC. You might consider trying a [version_no] series controller or combining a [product_name] PLC with a [company_name] building automation module, such as [article_no]. This module can convert a 0–10V input to PWM, but an 8kHz frequency remains quite high. It's possible the heater has its own power module with integrated control options. If you can provide a type number or share a document, perhaps we can assist further.

Thank you, [user_name]. The heater in question is an induction heater designed for resistive, inductive, and capacitive loads, heated in the medium frequency range due to stirring effects. As I developed the heater myself, I can reduce the target frequency range to 3kHz to 6kHz. The PLC will control trigger pulses sent to the gates of a single-phase inverter through a gate drive module that boosts voltage pulses. Warm regards, [user_name]
